newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel systems failure not cause of fire.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel systems failure not cause of fire.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, the Anglo-French Channel tunnel operator, said on Thursday an internal inquiry found that last November's fire was not caused by mechanical or systems failure of its equipment or rolling stock.
However, the inquiry did find that there were "avoidable delays in executing some of the (emergency) procedures" at the time of the fire.
Eurotunnel attributed the delays to the complexity of some of the procedures and to human and technical problems in communication.
The exact cause of the fire was still being investigated by French judicial authorities, the group said in a statement.
Eurotunnel said it had implemented a number of changes to improve safety and planned to re-open HGV shuttle services before the middle of June.
This would allow time for repairs to the south tunnel to be completed by mid-May, the firm said.
Last November's fire -- which caused no injuries to staff or passengers -- damaged a large section of the tunnel and severely hit passenger and freight services.
The group said it had implemented a number of changes in procedures, equipment, manning levels and training to improve safety.

The changes to improve fire prevention included more systematic checks on every lorry (truck) at the time of loading, better surveillance of departing shuttles, and more direct contact with the control centre.
Eurotunnel also planned to install additional fire suppression systems in the rail tunnels by 1999.

"The Channel Tunnel was designed to be one of the safest transport systems in the world. The changes we have announced today will make the system even safer and give us the confidence to re-open our HGV shuttle services," chairmen Patrick Ponsolle and Robert Malpas said in a statement.
Eurotunnel's shares were unchanged in London at 70.5 pence by 0815 GMT.
